prefix: - 2026-10-10 (Order 50, native-50 handed back; merged to next):

stamps.F126: DONE (native-50, 2614c183). `vilan_rt::Location` prints as its text at the top level, as JS does; inside a list or an Option the printer already wrote `<Location>` on both backends; interpolating a Location is refused by the checker on both, as before. Pin f126_print_of_a_location_writes_its_text_on_both_backends.
stamps.F128: DONE (native-50, d7d1b2f0). Premise half wrong: `filter`'s predicate takes the element by value, and the checker accepts `*` on a plain value (JS treats it as the value). A `*` over a by-value parameter, or a local whose initializer is clearly a value, now emits the value itself; a misjudged binding can only fail rustc, never change an answer. Pin f128_a_dereference_of_a_value_binding_reads_the_value_on_both_backends. Owner Q: should `*` on a plain value warn (R6 defines `*` on views only)? Rec: a non-breaking steer.
stamps.F127: DONE (native-50, 49cb53e9). A spread of a tuple literal contributes its parts directly, each written at its slot's type, evaluated once and in order, nested spreads included. Pin f127_a_spread_of_a_tuple_literal_is_its_parts_on_both_backends.
stamps.F125: DONE as a MISCOMPILE (native-50, f76a5e10): on 0.47.0 `i"{big * big}"` printed `144n` natively against JS's `144` (an operator's result records no type, so it fell to node's n-suffixed rendering). A BigInt in a concatenation now renders through `vilan_rt::bigint_text`. Pin f125_a_bigint_as_text_writes_its_digits_on_both_backends.
stamps.F123: DONE as a MISCOMPILE (native-50, de2a340b): `cell.read().seen.contains(mark(cell, "late"))` printed `false` natively, `true` on JS (the set was copied before the argument ran). HashSet::contains, HashMap::get and contains_key now read through the cell with the borrow taken after the arguments, when the key hashes with std's own code (scalars, str, BigInt, bool, and tuples/arrays/Lists of those); a user key type keeps the copy. F114's emission pin expects 0 copies. The general early-copy bug filed as F129.
stamps.F122: DONE (native-50, 9025b5e6). The array type stays `[T; N]`; past 1 KiB (element size x length) it renders as `vilan_rt::HeapArray<T, N>` (derefs to the array, built on the heap, cloned element by element; a plain Box<[T; N]> would still build its clone on the stack); a slot-by-slot pattern over such an array is refused by name. Threshold measured: an inline array costs 4-5 copies in its frame, a 1 KiB local recursed past 7000 frames natively (node fails at 5000-7000), 2 KiB overflowed at 5000. `[0; 4000000]` runs. Pin f122_a_fixed_array_past_one_kib_lives_on_the_heap_on_both_backends. Owner Q: keep 1 KiB? Rec yes.
stamps.F124: §2.1 and §2.2 DONE (native-50, 97b82fc8 + 9610e079). The emitter groups each root with its view bindings and walks each body once for access order. §2.1 nested intervals: the alias becomes a plain Rust reborrow (`&mut *b`), zero cost; builds every forwarding shape, flips no corpus program alone. §2.2 interleaved: the root moves into the Captured cell and each view is a handle on it; reads/writes/&mut calls/compound writes are momentary borrows (a compound write through a `borrows` call settles its value first). transparent-references.vl FLIPPED: the whole-set triple 130/127/3/0 -> 130/128/2/0 (async-await and signal-update remain). Refused by name: two loans of one promoted root in one call with one &mut; a view of a field/element/slot of an interleaved root; a view a closure names; a group in an async body; a view bound from a `borrows` call over a group member. Pins f124_a_nested_loan_group_reborrows_on_both_backends, f124_an_interleaved_loan_group_shares_one_cell_on_both_backends, f124_two_loans_in_one_call_and_a_projected_interleaved_view_are_refused_by_name. §2.3 (a lens handle `vilan_rt::Place<T>` for a view into part of a cell): owner Q, rec wait for a real program.
